findings.title: Charge is retried without an idempotency key, so customers can be double-charged
findings.explanation: A timeout or 502 does not mean the provider failed to process the charge. The request may have succeeded while the response was lost or a gateway failed. `createCharge` accepts an `idempotencyKey`, but it isn't passed here, so every retry is a new charge request. `withRetry` itself says it is only for idempotent operations (docs/CONVENTIONS.md). Fix: derive a stable key per payment attempt, for example from the invoice id plus a persisted attempt id, and pass it to `createCharge` on every retry. Reuse the same key when the user presses Pay again.

findings.title: Concurrent requests for the same invoice can charge twice
findings.explanation: The invoice is read with a plain SELECT, with no lock and no claim of the invoice. Two concurrent requests, such as a double click or a client retry while the server is still retrying for up to several seconds, can both see status 'open' and both charge. Retries make the window longer. Fix: claim the invoice before charging, using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or a status transition to 'processing'. Alternatively, use a stable per-invoice idempotency key together with a unique constraint on payments (invoice_id).

findings.title: Charge and DB writes are not atomic
findings.explanation: If the INSERT into payments or the UPDATE of the invoice fails after a successful charge, the customer has been charged but the invoice stays 'open' and can be paid again. This was already the case, but it is now worse because the route performs more provider calls. Fix: persist a pending payment before the charge, and reconcile afterwards. Wrap the INSERT and UPDATE in a transaction.

findings.title: Total latency and error handling after retries are exhausted
findings.explanation: With a 10s timeout per attempt, 3 attempts and backoff, the request can take over 30s. That may exceed the load balancer or client timeout, and the client will then retry on its own, creating more duplicate charges. Also, once retries are exhausted, the ProviderError propagates, and there is no handler in this route to map it to a clean 502/504 response. Fix: map ProviderError to a clear response, and consider a lower attempt count or an overall deadline.

findings.title: Backoff has no jitter and retries are not logged
findings.explanation: Add jitter to avoid synchronized retries during provider incidents. Log each retry with attempt number and error, without sensitive data, so the effect of this change can be measured. There are no tests covering the retry path in payments.

## Retry payment provider calls on transient errors

We see a handful of provider timeouts and 502s a day, and customers have to press Pay again. This wraps the charge call in our existing `withRetry` helper, which already retries timeouts and 5xx responses with backoff.
